rubric.why: Sabotage involves deliberate action, not accidental damage.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the action is intentional.

rubric.why: The answer must connect the deliberate damage to computer systems, data, or networks.
rubric.description: Identifies what is damaged or disrupted.
rubric.how: Award for naming computer systems, data, or a network.

modelAnswer: Sabotage is the deliberate damaging or disrupting of computer systems, data, or a network.

items.followUp: Name two types of communication media used to connect computers in a network.

rubric.why: Computers need a medium or channel to carry information between them.
rubric.description: States that computers are linked through a communication medium or channel.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning a communication medium, channel, or cable.

rubric.why: Examples or network equipment clarify how the connection is made.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable connection method or equipment.
rubric.how: Award for a suitable example such as cables, wireless links, or network devices.

modelAnswer: Computers in a network are connected through communication media, using wired links such as cables or wireless links.
Network devices and network interface hardware help establish the connection and allow computers to communicate.

items.followUp: Write one example of an IPv4 address.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a switch and a hub?

rubric.why: A switch or hub links multiple devices on a network.
rubric.description: States that a switch or hub connects network devices.
rubric.how: Award for identifying its role in connecting computers or devices.

rubric.why: The connected devices use the switch or hub to communicate.
rubric.description: States that it enables communication or data transfer.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning communication or data transmission between connected devices.

modelAnswer: A switch or hub is used to connect several computers or other devices in a local area network.
It allows the connected devices to communicate and exchange data.

rubric.why: A multipoint connection is shared by multiple devices.
rubric.description: Explains that multiple devices share one connection or link.
rubric.how: Award for stating that more than two devices use the same link.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates where this connection is used.
rubric.description: Gives an appropriate example or application.
rubric.how: Award for an example such as a bus network topology or a shared communication link.

modelAnswer: A multipoint connection is used when more than two devices share a single communication link.
For example, it is used in a bus network topology.

items.followUp: What does the COLOR attribute of the BODY tag specify?

rubric.description: Identifies the TEXT attribute and its purpose.

It specifies the colour of the text displayed on the web page.

items.followUp: Define a flowchart and state two advantages and two disadvantages.

rubric.why: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
rubric.description: Defines an algorithm as an ordered procedure for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Award for describing a sequence of steps or instructions to solve a problem.

rubric.why: These are standard advantages of using algorithms.
rubric.how: Award for listing three valid advantages, such as being easy to understand, language-independent, and helpful in finding errors.

rubric.why: Algorithms can be tedious to prepare and are less convenient for complex problems; the question requests disadvantages as well as advantages.
rubric.how: Award both marks for listing three valid disadvantages, such as being time-consuming to write, lengthy for complex problems, and lacking a standard format.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step sequence of instructions for solving a problem.
Advantages:
1. It is easy to understand and communicate.
2. It helps to find and correct errors before coding.
3. It is independent of any particular programming language.
Disadvantages:
1. Writing an algorithm can be time-consuming.
2. Algorithms for complex problems can become lengthy and difficult to follow.
3. There is no single standard format for writing algorithms.
